# Mud dyeing (iron mud on tannin-treated cloth)

## 8. Models

<!-- models:start (generated by tools/process_models.mjs; edit outside these markers) -->

### Mudcloth (`lumenary:mudcloth`, models this process)

_From: The Bamana of Mali; when: Centuries old; works best on: Pictures with distinct light and dark regions._

Bogolanfini, mud cloth, is made by painting cloth with mud that has fermented for months. The iron in the mud reacts with tannin in the cloth to make a black that does not wash out. Here each tone of the picture is given its own motif, from bare cloth through dots, zigzags and crosses to solid mud, so the picture becomes a pattern of patterns.

**How it is made, as the model does it:**

1. Set a level from 0 to 4 that rises with the picture’s darkness, and keep regions clean with a majority filter.
2. Give each level its own motif: bare cloth, dots, zigzag rows, crosses, and solid mud pricked with small holes.
3. Where two levels meet, clear the pattern within about 3.4 px of the boundary and draw a mud line about 1 px on either side.
4. Add a hand-painted wobble to every stroke.
5. Sew the cloth in narrow strips, with visible seams, as it is woven.

**The maths:**

$$\ell=\min\big(4,\ \lfloor 5\,v\rfloor\big),\qquad v=1-L\ \ (\text{or } L \text{ if inverted})$$

_The level from the blurred brightness L._ (primitives: tone-bands)

$$\bar m_\ell\approx\{\,0,\ 0.07,\ 0.26,\ 0.41,\ 0.955\,\}$$

_The share of cloth the motif of each level covers: nothing; dots of radius 0.15 q; a band 0.26 q wide; a cross with arms 0.3 q × 0.84 q; and solid mud with holes of radius 0.12 q._ (written for this model: constants)

$$m_2:\ \Big|\operatorname{frac}\!\Big(\tfrac{y+\frac{q}{2}\tau}{q}\Big)-\tfrac12\Big|<0.13,\qquad \tau=2\,\Big|\operatorname{frac}\tfrac{x}{q}-\tfrac12\Big|$$

_The zigzag motif: a band bent by the triangle wave τ._ (primitives: lattice-repeat)

**Dials:** `size` (Motif size) = 12 [6 to 24]; `smooth` (Simplify) = 5 [1 to 10]; `outline` (Outlines) = 70 [0 to 100]; `hand` (Hand-painted wobble) = 55 [0 to 100]; `strips` (Strip seams) = true; `cloth` (Cloth) = "cream" (cream, ochre, rust); `invert` (Mud on the light) = false.

**History:** The Bamana weave cotton in narrow strips, soak it in a tea of leaves rich in tannin, paint patterns with fermented mud and then bleach the background. The designs often carry meanings of history, proverbs and protection. In the late twentieth century the Malian designer Chris Seydou brought bogolan into fashion, and it is now worn around the world.
